symptom: A `[%Token%]` with a name Mendix does not have — a typo ([%CurrentDateTim%], [%CurentDateTime%]), a non-token ([%BeginOfCurrentQuarter%], [%Today%], [%CurrentDeviceType%]) or a context-only one ([%DayLength%] in a flow, [%CurrentObject%] in a retrieve) — passed check -p --references and exec; mx check 11.14.0 reported CE0117 in an expression and CE0161 in an XPath (ako/mxcli#2271).
cause: The lexer reads any [%...%] as MENDIX_TOKEN and no validator read the name: #1723 checked only the role after UserRole_, #2189 only the type of a few token families in access rules.
file: mdl/executor/validate_token_names.go (new, MDL-TOKEN01, wired in ValidateProgram), mdl/executor/validate_access_rule_xpath.go (xpathDateTokenRE = tokenDateRe)
insight: Measure the vocabulary, then probe its neighbours: the documented list alone missed (Begin|End)Of(Tomorrow|Yesterday)[UTC], found only by probing ~80 plausible names (Next/Previous/Last/Quarter/Today...) of which that family was the only valid one — shipping the documented list would have refused valid scripts. Validate the rule against the measurement, not just the cases: re-running check over every probe and diffing with mx check's per-document JSON (mx check -j) gave 307/307 agreement and caught the one deliberate gap (CurrentObject in a retrieve). Remove CE1613-producing probes first: a CE1613 in the app suppresses every CE0117/CE0161 (the #1723 finding), which turned the first 98-flow run into 2 errors.
